name: Fortiva Credit Card
perks: Unsecured card with no security deposit required
Prequalification uses a soft pull that does not affect your score
Reports to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion)
Free VantageScore credit score access through the account portal
The separate Fortiva Cash Back Rewards version earns 3% on gas, groceries, and utilities and 1% elsewhere, if that is the offer you receive
drawbacks: Annual fee is $49 to $175 the first year, then $0 to $49 plus a $5 to $12.50 monthly fee starting in year two (up to about $199 per year), as of mid-2026; Fortiva assigns terms per applicant, so read your exact offer
Fee math: a $175 first-year fee on a $350 starting limit consumes 50% of your available credit before your first purchase
Purchase APR of 29.99% or 36% depending on the offer, among the highest available
The standard card earns no rewards at all
Serviced by Atlanticus for The Bank of Missouri, a program with a long record of fee and servicing complaints
A Capital One Platinum Secured needs as little as a $49 refundable deposit and charges $0 a year forever; over three years that is $0 versus up to roughly $573 in Fortiva fees
Verdict: skip the standard Fortiva card; if you somehow receive the rare low-fee Cash Back offer it becomes tolerable, but a secured card or Mission Lane is the better move for almost everyone
